mainTopic: ריבית and benefits in prepaid deals, the king's law, and a negligent agent's אסמכתא
overview: This amud brings a series of short stories and rulings about ריבית and about using other people's money or work. A גוי mortgaged a house to רב מרי בר רחל and then sold it to רבא. רבא refused רב מרי's rent and kept the גוי's original deal. רב אשי explains that paying for wine in תשרי and choosing it in טבת is not ריבית, because the buyers only receive the wine they paid for. He also permits an extra jug that sellers freely give רבינא, because by the king's law those sellers own the produce. In the same way, רבא quotes רב ששת that the king's law lets someone who pays another person's head tax make that person work for him. רבא also approves of his brother רב סעורם forcing misbehaving people to carry his chair, based on a ברייתא from a פסוק. Finally, רב חמא rules that a negligent agent who failed to buy wine pays the market price, and רב זביד limits this to general wine. רב אשי disagrees completely, calling it an אסמכתא, and the גמרא explains why a sharecropper's promise is different: there, the outcome is in his own hands.

steps.title: A mortgaged house is sold to רבא
steps.stepSummary: A גוי mortgages a house to רב מרי בר רחל, sells it to רבא, and after a year רב מרי brings rent to רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain גוי mortgaged a house to רב מרי בר רחל. Then the גוי sold the house to רבא. רב מרי waited twelve months, took rent money for the house, and brought it to רבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a story and sets up the facts. The next step explains why רב מרי waited a year before paying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב מרי lent money to a גוי and received the house as security, with the right to live in it. When רבא bought the house, the lender became a Jew living in a Jew's house. Living there for free in exchange for a loan could look like ריבית.

keyTerms.meaning: gave as a mortgage (security for a loan)

phrases.english: Rav Mari bar Rachel
a certain gentile mortgaged a house to him.
phrases.notes: The גוי borrowed money from רב מרי and gave him the house as security.

phrases.english: Then he sold it to Rava.
He waited twelve months of the year,
took the rent for the house,
and brought it to Rava.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב מָרִי בַּר רָחֵל מַשְׁכֵּן לֵיהּ הָהוּא גּוֹי בֵּיתָא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Jew who holds a mortgaged house that now belongs to another Jew offers rent to avoid ריבית.

steps.title: רב מרי explains why he waited a year
steps.stepSummary: רב מרי says a mortgage with no stated term lasts one year, so the house was his until now. From now on he should pay rent.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מרי said to רבא: I did not bring you rent until now because a mortgage with no stated term lasts one year. During that year, even if the גוי wanted to pay me back and remove me, he could not. Now, please take rent for the house.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מרי explains his reasoning. During the first year the house was fully his, but now it has to be treated as רבא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the borrower could not remove him during the first year, the house was really his for that year, so living there was not ריבית. After that year the owner can pay back the loan at any time. Living there for free now would be a benefit he gets because of the loan, so he offers rent.

keyTerms.meaning: a mortgage with no stated time period
to remove (by paying back the loan)

phrases.english: He said to him:
The reason I did not bring the Master
the rent for the house until now
is that an unspecified mortgage lasts a year,
so if the gentile had wanted to remove me,
he could not have removed me.
Now, let the Master take the rent for the house.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי דְּלָא אַמְטַאי לְמָר אֲגַר בֵּיתָא עַד הָאִידָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind רב מרי's actions in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A mortgage with no stated term cannot be ended during its first year. After the year passes, living in the house for free could be ריבית.

steps.title: רבא refuses the rent and follows the rules that applied to the גוי
steps.stepSummary: רבא says he would not have bought the house had he known it was mortgaged. He will step into the גוי's place and take no rent until the loan is paid off. As רש״י explains, he means he will make the גוי pay it; רבא himself owes nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Had I known the house was mortgaged to you, I would not have bought it. So now I will treat you by their law: as long as they have not paid the lender back, they take no rent. I too will not take rent from you until I have you paid off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers רב מרי's offer and refuses the rent. He says he stepped into the גוי's place, so the gentile arrangement stays in force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sees himself as taking over the deal exactly as the גוי made it. Under that arrangement, the lender lives there for free until the loan is paid off. רבא keeps the original deal and does not create a new rental agreement between two Jews.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא did not take rent. He stepped into the גוי's place and kept the original free-living arrangement until the loan would be paid.
steps.confusionAlert: The story starts with רב מרי offering rent to avoid ריבית. רבא is the one who refuses it, not רב מרי.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Had I known
that it was mortgaged to the Master,
I would not have bought it.
Now I will act toward you according to their law:
phrases.notes: "Their law" means the rules that applied to the גוי who made the deal.

phrases.english: as long as they have not removed him with money,
phrases.notes: "Removing with money" means paying off the loan so the lender has to leave the house.

phrases.english: he does not take rent for the house.

phrases.aramaic: אֲנָא נָמֵי לָא שָׁקֵילְנָא מִינָּךְ אֲגַר בֵּיתָא
phrases.english: I too will not take rent for the house from you
until I remove you with money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הֲוָה יָדַעְנָא דַּהֲוָה מְמוּשְׁכַּן לֵיהּ לְמָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to רב מרי's offer of rent in step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Should רבא take rent from רב מרי now that the first year is over?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. רבא follows the deal the גוי made and takes no rent until the loan is paid off (as רש״י explains, by making the גוי pay it).

steps.title: רבא מברניש says the רבנן seem to take interest with wine
steps.stepSummary: רבא מברניש points out that the רבנן pay for wine in תשרי but pick it out only in טבת, which looks like ריבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מברניש said to רב אשי: Look at the רבנן who eat ריבית! They pay money for wine in תשרי and choose their wine only in טבת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. רבא מברניש challenges a common practice of the רבנן as a hidden form of ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By waiting until טבת to choose, the buyers can see which wine has turned to vinegar and avoid it. He argues that this protection is an extra benefit they get for paying early, and that makes it ריבית.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִבַּרְנִישׁ לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava of Barnish said to Rav Ashi:
Let the Master look at the Rabbis
who are eating interest,
for they give money for wine in Tishrei
and select it in Tevet!
phrases.notes: By טבת, wine that is going to spoil has already turned, so they can avoid the bad barrels.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי מָר רַבָּנַן דְּקָא אָכְלִי רִבִּיתָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of paying for wine in תשרי and choosing it in טבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer gains protection from spoilage because he paid early, and an extra benefit in return for early payment looks like ריבית.

steps.title: רב אשי: They bought wine, and later they only choose it
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the deal was always for wine and never for vinegar. Choosing later only reveals which barrels were wine from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to him: They paid for wine, not for vinegar. From the beginning, what was wine was wine and what was vinegar was vinegar. It is only at that later time that they choose.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי defends the רבנן and explains why this is not ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The buyers paid for good wine. Barrels that later turn out to be vinegar were never part of what they bought. Waiting until טבת gives no extra benefit; it only lets them receive exactly what they paid for.
steps.whatToRemember: Paying early and choosing later is not ריבית, because the buyer only receives the wine he paid for. Spoiled wine was never part of the sale.

phrases.english: He said to him:
They, too, gave money for wine;
they did not give it for vinegar.
From the start, what was wine was wine,
and what was vinegar was vinegar;
phrases.notes: He means that wine which later turns sour was already headed that way when they paid, even though no one knew it yet.

phrases.english: it is only at that time that they select.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינְהוּ נָמֵי אַחַמְרָא קָא יָהֲבִי, אַחַלָּא לָא קָא יָהֲבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of רבא מברניש in step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the transaction: the sale was for good wine from the start, so waiting gives no extra benefit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Choosing later is a benefit received in exchange for paying early, which would make it ריבית.
steps.terutzMaskana: The buyer only receives the wine he already bought. Choosing later is not an extra benefit, so it is not ריבית.

steps.title: רבינא gets an extra jug of wine and asks if it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבינא paid ahead of time for wine, and the sellers poured him an extra jug. He asks רב אשי whether this is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא used to give money to the people of the fortress at שנוותא, and they would pour him an extra jug. He came before רב אשי and asked: Is this allowed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a new story about a prepaid wine deal. רבינא asks רב אשי whether the extra jug he receives is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying first and getting the goods later can look like a loan. If so, getting back more than he paid would look like ריבית. That is why רבינא is worried about the extra jug.

keyTerms.meaning: A jug or measure of wine

phrases.english: Ravina would give money
phrases.notes: He paid in advance, before the wine was delivered.

phrases.english: to the people of the fortress of Shanvata
and they would pour him an extra jug.
He came before Rav Ashi.
He said to him: Is it permitted?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new story on the same theme of prepaying for wine (compare Step 4) and the fear of ריבית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the extra jug forbidden as ריבית on the advance payment?

steps.title: רב אשי: yes, they are simply giving it to you
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says it is allowed, because the sellers are freely giving up the extra wine as a gift.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes. They are simply giving it up to you as a favor.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers that the extra jug is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra wine is not payment for the early money. The sellers give it on their own as goodwill, so it is a gift and not ריבית.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
they are simply waiving it in your favor.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִין, אַחוֹלֵי הוּא דְּקָא מָחֲלִי גַּבָּךְ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Permitted, because the extra jug is a free gift (מחילה) and not payment for the advance.

steps.title: But the land does not belong to them
steps.stepSummary: רבינא pushes back: how can they give away wine from land that is not theirs?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But the land is not theirs!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges רב אשי's answer. A person can only give away what he owns.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These farmers were working fields that belonged to other people. If the grapes are not theirs, they cannot give the extra jug as a gift. Then the gift reason would fall apart.

phrases.english: He said to him: But the land
is not theirs!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אַרְעָא לָאו דִּידְהוּ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the gift reason given in Step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the sellers are giving up the extra wine as a gift
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: You can only give a gift from what you own. These farmers do not own the land, so the wine may not be theirs to give.

steps.title: The king's law gives the land to whoever pays the tax
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי explains that the land is held for the king's tax. The king rules that whoever pays the tax eats from the land, so the wine is theirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The land is tied to the tax. And the king says: Whoever pays the tax may eat from the land.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the challenge. The farmers do own the produce by the king's law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owners left because they could not pay the land tax. The king rules that the produce goes to whoever pays the tax. Since these farmers pay it, the wine is legally theirs, and they can give some away.

phrases.english: He said to him: The land is pledged for the tax.
And the king says:
Whoever pays the tax may eat from the land.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a legal fact (the king's law) that settles who owns the produce
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The farmers are only working someone else's land, so the wine is not theirs to give.
steps.terutzMaskana: By the king's law, whoever pays the tax owns the produce. So the farmers own the wine and may give the extra jug as a gift.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the king's law (דינא דמלכותא) can decide who owns property, and that decision matters for the laws of ריבית.

steps.title: רב פפא objects to Sages who pay people's taxes and then make them work
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא complains to רבא about רבנן who pay other people's head tax and then make those people work for them, more than seems fair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to רבא: Look, Master, at these רבנן who pay money for people's head tax and then make them work too much!
steps.whatsHappening: A new case. רב פפא is troubled that רבנן pay someone's head tax and then make that person work hard for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Paying someone's tax looks like a loan. Getting a lot of work back in return could look like ריבית, or even like forcing a fellow Jew to work like a slave.

keyTerms.meaning: Head tax (a tax on each person)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Rava:
Let the Master see these Sages
who give money for people's head tax
and make them work more than that!

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲזִי מָר הָנֵי רַבָּנַן דְּיָהֲבִי זוּזֵי אַכְּרָגָא דְּאִינָשֵׁי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new case that, like Step 9, will be settled by the king's tax law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of the רבנן who pay people's head tax and then use their work
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Getting more work back than the money paid looks like ריבית, or like an unfair way of using a fellow Jew.

steps.title: רבא quotes רב ששת: the king's law makes them serve the one who pays
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers with what רב ששת said. These people are like the king's servants, and the king ruled that whoever does not pay the head tax must serve whoever pays it.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If I had died, I could not have told you this. This is what רב ששת said: The servant-documents of these people lie in the king's treasury. And the king said: Whoever does not pay the head tax shall serve whoever pays it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends the רבנן. By the king's law, they are allowed to make these people work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The work is not repayment for a loan. It comes from the king's own law, which gives the person who did not pay over to serve the person who paid. So there is no ריבית and no wrongdoing.

phrases.english: He said to him: Now, if I had died,
I could not have told you this matter.
phrases.notes: He means: it is good you asked me while I'm alive, because I know the answer.

phrases.english: This is what Rav Sheshet said:
The servant-documents of these people lie in the king's treasury,
phrases.notes: In other words, every subject is counted as the king's servant.

phrases.english: and the king said:
Whoever does not pay the head tax
shall serve whoever pays the head tax!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: מוּהְרְקַיְיהוּ דְּהָנֵי בְּטֻפְסָא דְמַלְכָּא מַנַּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's objection in Step 10, using the same kind of king's law as Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The king's law creates the right to the person's work
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The work is extra payment for money laid out, so it looks like ריבית or misuse.
steps.terutzMaskana: The king's law gives the right to the work. It is not payment for a loan.
steps.whatToRemember: In both the wine case and the head-tax case, the king's law (דינא דמלכותא) decides the matter. It makes the farmers the owners of the produce, and it makes the people who did not pay the tax serve the ones who paid it.

steps.title: רב סעורם forces misbehaving people to carry רבא's chair
steps.stepSummary: רב סעורם, רבא's brother, would grab people who behaved badly and make them carry רבא's chair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב סעורם, the brother of רבא, would seize people who did not behave properly and make them carry רבא's chair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells another story about making people work. This one is about people who behave badly. It sets up רבא's reaction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the work does not come from a tax payment. It is forced on people because of how they act. So the question is whether it is ever allowed to make a Jew serve like this.

phrases.english: Rav Se'oram, the brother of Rava,
would seize people who did not behave properly
and put them under Rava's carried chair.
phrases.notes: Meaning he made them carry the chair.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב סְעוּרָם אֲחוּהּ דְּרָבָא הֲוָה תָּקֵיף אִינָשֵׁי דְּלָא מְעַלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related story about making people work, but here the reason is bad behavior, not a tax.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A story that sets up the question: may you make a misbehaving Jew work for you?

steps.title: רבא approves and brings a ברייתא from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב סעורם he acted correctly. He brings a ברייתא: you may make a Jew who behaves badly work for you, but not one who behaves properly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: You did well. As we learned: If you see someone who does not behave properly, how do we know you may make him serve you? The פסוק says: 'Forever you may make them serve, and over your brothers.' Could it be even if he behaves properly? The פסוק says: 'And over your brothers, the children of Israel, one over another...' you may not rule harshly.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא supports his brother's practice with a ברייתא. The ברייתא learns from a פסוק that it is allowed, but only for someone who behaves badly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The extra word 'and' in 'and over your brothers' links Jews to the first half of the פסוק about making slaves serve. That teaches that sometimes a Jew may be made to serve. The end of the פסוק forbids ruling over a brother, and the ברייתא reads it as protecting a Jew who behaves properly.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not permission to make any Jew serve you. The ברייתא itself limits it to someone who does not behave properly. A Jew who behaves properly is fully protected by the end of the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: שַׁפִּיר קָא עָבְדַתְּ, דִּתְנֵינָא:
phrases.english: Rava said to him: You are acting well, as we learned:
If you saw him not behaving properly,
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is the corrected wording, so read it as 'you saw him.'

phrases.english: how do we know that you are permitted to make him serve you?
The verse teaches:
"Forever you may make them serve, and over your brothers."
One might think, even if he behaves properly?
The verse teaches:
"And over your brothers, the children of Israel, one over another, etc."
phrases.notes: The פסוק goes on: you shall not rule over him harshly.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: שַׁפִּיר קָא עָבְדַתְּ, דִּתְנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבא's approval of the practice in Step 12, with a source.
steps.raayaObject: רב סעורם's practice of making misbehaving people carry רבא's chair
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading ויקרא 25:46: the word 'and over your brothers' allows it, and the end of the פסוק limits it to someone who does not behave properly.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the limit. Forcing a Jew to serve is allowed only for someone who does not behave properly. It is never allowed for someone who acts as he should.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: One may make a Jew who behaves badly serve, but one may not rule over a Jew who behaves properly.

steps.title: A negligent agent pays the market price of wine
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא rules that an agent who took money to buy wine, was negligent, and did not buy it must pay according to the wine price in the port of זולשפט.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא said: If someone gives money to a friend to buy wine for him, and the friend is negligent and does not buy it, the friend must pay him based on the going price of wine at the port of זולשפט.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ruling from רב חמא about an agent who failed to buy wine as he was asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent does not simply return the money. He must give the buyer the value of the wine at the main market price, even if wine has since become more expensive. His negligence made him responsible for the wine the buyer should have had.

keyTerms.meaning: Money (literally: zuzim, a type of coin)

phrases.english: Rav Chama said:
One who gives money to his friend
to buy wine for him
and he was negligent and did not buy it for him –
he pays him according to the going rate
at the port of Zolshefat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of tax and servants.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A negligent agent who failed to buy wine must pay the buyer at the market price of wine in זולשפט.

steps.title: The ruling applies only to wine in general, not one specific wine
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד limits רב חמא's ruling to a request for wine in general. If the buyer asked for one specific wine, the agent does not pay, because the seller might never have sold it.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: I told this teaching to רב זביד of נהרדעא, and he said: When רב חמא said this, it was only about a request for "wine" in general. But if the buyer said "this wine," the agent does not pay. Who says the owner would have sold it to him?
steps.whatsHappening: רב זביד narrows רב חמא's ruling to cases where the buyer asked for any wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: General wine can always be bought on the market, so the agent's negligence truly caused the loss. With one specific wine, the owner might have refused to sell it. In that case the buyer cannot say the agent cost him the wine, so the agent just returns the money.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: I said this teaching
before Rav Zevid of Neharde'a,
and he said: When Rav Chama said this,
that applies to "wine" without specifying,
but with "this wine" – no,
who says they would have sold it to him?

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי קָאָמַר רַב חָמָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב חמא's ruling to a request for general wine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב חמא's ruling applies only to general wine. For a specific wine, the agent does not pay the market price.

steps.title: Even for wine in general the agent does not pay, because it is an אסמכתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי says the agent does not pay even for general wine. Paying more than he received would be an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not make a binding commitment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even for "wine" in general, the agent does not pay. What is the reason? It is an אסמכתא, and an אסמכתא does not bind.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues with רב חמא completely and says the agent never has to pay more than the money he was given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The agent never seriously meant to pay extra if he failed. Any extra payment rests on a commitment he did not truly accept. Such a half-hearted commitment, called an אסמכתא, has no legal force, so the agent only returns the money.

keyTerms.meaning: A commitment made without full intent, assuming it will never have to be paid
Does not bind (literally: does not acquire)

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not only arguing with רב זביד's limit. He rejects רב חמא's ruling even in the general-wine case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This brings the important rule that an אסמכתא does not bind into the case, and the rest of the discussion tests that rule.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Even with "wine" without specifying, also not,
what is the reason? It is an asmachta,
and an asmachta does not bind.
phrases.notes: Literally, "does not acquire." He means the commitment has no legal force.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר אֲפִילּוּ יַיִן סְתָם נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רב זביד and rejects רב חמא's ruling completely.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רב חמא's ruling even for general wine.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Paying more than he received would rest on an אסמכתא, which does not bind.

steps.title: Challenge from the sharecropper who promised to pay with the best produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רב אשי's view differs from the משנה where a sharecropper writes that if he leaves the field unworked, he will pay with the best produce. There, the promise does bind.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רב אשי, how is this different from what we learned in a משנה: "If I leave the field unworked and do not work it, I will pay with the best"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with a משנה where a promise to pay for a possible failure does seem to bind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sharecropper promised to pay if he failed to do his job, just like the agent. The משנה treats his promise as binding, not as an אסמכתא. So why should the agent's commitment be an אסמכתא?

keyTerms.meaning: I will leave the field unworked (fallow)

phrases.english: And according to Rav Ashi, what is different
from that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה later in this מסכת about renting out a field to a sharecropper.

phrases.english: "If I leave it fallow and do not work it,
I will pay with the best",

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב אָשֵׁי מַאי שְׁנָא מֵהָא דִּתְנַן
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that the agent's commitment is an אסמכתא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sharecropper's promise to pay if he fails to work is binding, so a similar promise by the agent should bind too.

steps.title: There, the outcome is in his own hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the sharecropper's case is different because whether he works the field is completely up to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is in his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing to a difference between the sharecropper and the agent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sharecropper fully controls whether he works the field. So he meant his promise seriously, and it is not an אסמכתא. The answer suggests the agent's case is different because he does not fully control the result.

keyTerms.meaning: In his hands, under his control

phrases.english: There, it is in his hands,
phrases.notes: He means the sharecropper alone decides whether to work the field.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: control over the outcome
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sharecropper's binding promise shows the agent's promise should bind too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The sharecropper's promise binds because the outcome is fully in his control, so it is not an אסמכתא.
